correctness.rationale: Exact Gaussian-tail identity and uniform remainder |E_L(xi)|<=1/(4L^2) control the oscillatory boundary layer in C^1. Global Fourier Gaussian-minus-tail comparison proves no earlier zeros; one full oscillation produces a sign change beyond the onset. The exceptional double phase is determined by two scalar equations and is proven to be the first limiting tangency. Fixed-cutoff integration by parts yields eventually one simple zero per sine lobe. High-precision quadrature and exact-error-function replay give independent finite checks, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A sharp, natural first-real-zero threshold for a hard-windowed Gaussian is essential to distinguishing a practical Gaussian approximation from its nominally zero-free full transform. The logarithmic boundary layer and nontrivial phase-selected microscopic first-root map locate the actual cancellation onset; a unique exceptional quadratic tangency produces a structurally meaningful boundary case. The result goes beyond finite checks and beyond previously known simple sector nonvanishing.
